label: Outcomes
description: Outcomes dataflow alone cannot state. `refuse` ends the graph on purpose: the branch a decision routed here is a declared refusal, not a bug. It names its outcome with a `reason`, one word the trigger kind maps to an answer; the graph never says how the trigger answers. A node that breaks where the graph declares nothing is a fault, which a data graph's switch may `catch` and route here.

refuse.description: Refuse: the graph fails on purpose. `reason` is one word for the outcome (missing, conflict, upstream), written as a literal so the checker can see every reason a trigger may reach and require the kind to map each (T005); `message`, {{templates}} in it reading what any value may, is what the caller is told. Answers nothing, but declares a type so it can stand as an out.from candidate opposite the node that answers. A rehearsal reports it as refused on purpose.

reason.description: one word for the outcome; the trigger kind maps it to how it answers (an http route: to a status)

message.description: what is said to the caller

type.description: the type the answering candidate has
